thread:
Alex (customer): Hey team — CI deploy to staging started failing this morning. All deploy jobs hit a 403 from Redwood API during the final push step. Worked yesterday.

Lina (support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the pipeline log excerpt and the exact error from the API?

Alex (customer): here's the curl from the failing step:

```
$ curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploys/staging/push
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "message": "token missing required scope: deploy:write"
}
```

And the pipeline shows the token was minted by `pipeline-service-bot` via our CI credentials. Looks like the token was accepted but rejected for scope.

Maya (infra): @Lina can you confirm if any RBAC changes went out? We didn't push org-wide policy changes but I did merge a PR to tighten some default SA scopes last week.

Lina (support): No org policy change recorded in tickets, but let me reproduce quickly. Which job step is failing?

Alex (customer): step `push-artifacts` (runs `redwoodctl deploy push --env staging`). It's a single command run after the build.

pipeline-bot: step push-artifacts failed with exit code 1 — API responded 403 (insufficient_scope).

Jon (eng-sre): Two likely classes: 1) the service account's assigned scopes got narrowed and deploy:write removed, or 2) the token minted by CI is short-lived and some intermediate retry/parallel step is reusing an expired token and Redwood returns insufficient_scope as a generic auth failure.

Maya (infra): quick check: I pulled the SA policy for `pipeline-service-bot` -> roles: [model:invoke, storage:read]. No deploy:write. That explains the explicit message. The merge last week set the default pipeline SA to read-only unless you opt into deploy. 

Lina (support): Okay so that matches the error text exactly. Would you prefer we add deploy:write to the SA or create a dedicated `deploy-service-bot` with just deploy rights?

Alex (customer): Prefer least-privilege. I'd rather have a separate bot solely for deploys. But we need a quick patch to unblock staging deploys today.

Jon (eng-sre): Short-term fix: add `deploy:write` to `pipeline-service-bot` for the staging namespace only, and revert to separate deploy SA as a follow-up. Also add a guard in the pipeline to fail fast if token scope doesn't include required perms.

Maya (infra): I'll apply a scoped change to staging only. Patch command I plan to run: 

```
# grant deploy permission scoped to staging
redwoodctl iam grant pipeline-service-bot --scope "deploy:write:env:staging"
```

Alex (customer): That would unblock. Also noticed token_ttl on our CI was set to 300s — sometimes the build takes >5m and we spawn parallel steps that inherit the same token. Do we recommend longer TTL for CI or OIDC flow?

Lina (support): We recommend OIDC where possible. For short-term, increasing token TTL to 1800s (30m) is fine, but it's not ideal security-wise. Better: use ephemeral OIDC tokens minted per-job step and avoid reusing a long-lived CI token.

Maya (infra): Repro steps I ran locally to confirm:
1) create token with only model:invoke and storage:read
2) run `redwoodctl deploy push` -> get 403 insufficient_scope
3) grant deploy:write for staging -> same command succeeds

Log snippet from repro: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z push-artifacts started
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z POST /v1/deploys -> 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token missing required scope: deploy:write"}
```

Jon (eng-sre): Proposed follow-ups (tickets):
- infra: create `deploy-service-bot` with minimal `deploy:write` and `audit:emit` perms, SC-4553 (owner: Maya)
- eng: add pipeline guard that checks token scopes before running critical steps, PL-4612 (owner: Jon)
- support: improve error doc to map insufficient_scope -> likely SA scope misconfig, SUP-2107 (owner: Lina)

Alex (customer): Sounds good. Can we also add a small script to detect this in pipelines so other teams don't hit it?

Maya (infra): yep adding snippet to our CI library: 

```
# ci/check-sa-scope.sh
TOKEN=$1
REQUIRED_SCOPE="$2"
RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token/introspect)
# quick jq-free parse
if echo "$RESPONSE" | grep -q "$REQUIRED_SCOPE"; then
  echo "scope ok"
  exit 0
else
  echo "missing scope: $REQUIRED_SCOPE" >&2
  exit 2
fi
```

Lina (support): I'll update the customer-facing KB with the repro and the exact error mapping. Also leaving a note to set an alert on spikes of 403 insufficient_scope from /v1/deploys endpoint.

Alex (customer): Thanks — staging deploys are green now after the scoped grant. Please do the follow-ups.

Maya (infra): Patch applied to staging: `deploy:write:env:staging` granted to pipeline-service-bot. Will start work on creating dedicated deploy SA and CI library check. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:

Jon (eng-sre): I'll add a quick pipeline step to assert scope presence before critical steps and open PL-4612.

deploy-bot: deployment attempt 2026-03-15T10:45:12Z succeeded for staging (post-grant). :party-parrot:

Lina (support): Marking thread resolved for now. Will update SUP-2107 when KB is live. :white_check_mark:
